battle.name: 波斯尼亞戰爭
battle.brief: 波斯尼亞戰爭於一九九二年爆發，塞拉耶佛隨市區與外圍據點的爭奪形成長期戰線。此一線膛砲（Muzzle-loading field gun）屬十九世紀野戰炮兵裝備，位於營級火力支援與攻城部署之間，雖非波斯尼亞戰爭所用主力，仍是理解當時炮兵體系角色的真實歷史裝備。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛砲在十九世紀德意志諸邦陸軍中屬野戰炮兵，配置於步兵營或旅級支援，承擔隨軍支援與封鎖射擊，並非軍級攻城重砲。

countries: 1992年的波斯尼亞戰線由四個相互重疊的軍政集團構成：波黑政府及其波黑共和國軍、克羅埃西亞國防委員會與受其支援的克羅埃西亞軍、由南斯拉夫人民軍波黑部隊和塞族地方武裝整合而成的塞族共和國軍，以及在撤出前仍參與作戰的南斯拉夫人民軍。克羅埃西亞與南斯拉夫是主要外部支援方，聯合國保護區部隊則是唯一獲准在三方之間部署並監督停火線的國際武裝。地理上，戰場沿既有公路、鐵路、河流與山脊分區，沙拉熱窩盆地、比哈奇盆地、波蘇什耶走廊、德里納河岸及內姆港附近海岸同時成為戰線。這些地形直接決定砲兵射界、補給速度、車輛通行與突擊方向。戰局由4月沙拉熱窩衝突展開，至年底轉成沙拉熱窩封鎖、比哈奇解圍與西部邊境三個相互牽動的主要戰區，並延續至1993年。
countriesEn: The 1992 Bosnian theater was formed by four overlapping military-political actors: the Bosnian government and the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Croatian Defence Council and the Croatian forces supporting it, the Army of Republika Srpska created from Yugoslav People's Army formations in Bosnia and local Serb forces, and the Yugoslav People's Army itself while it was still withdrawing. Croatia and Yugoslavia were the principal external supporters, while the United Nations Protection Force was the only international armed force authorized to deploy among the three parties and monitor ceasefire lines. Geographically, the battlefield was divided by existing roads, railways, rivers, and ridges. The Sarajevo basin, the Bihać basin, the Posušje corridor, the Drina riverbank, and the coast near the port of Neum all became operational theaters. These features directly determined artillery sightlines, resupply speeds, vehicle movement, and the direction of attacks. The conflict began with the fighting in Sarajevo in April and evolved by year-end into three interconnected operational areas: the siege of Sarajevo, the efforts to relieve Bihać, and the western border front. It then continued into 1993.
people: 波斯尼亞衝突的指揮權始終分散於政治領袖、軍隊總參謀長與前南軍指揮官之間。波黑主席團主席阿里雅·伊澤特貝戈維奇代表國家的統一制憲目標；塞族民主黨領袖拉多萬·卡拉季奇則主持塞族地方機構的建立，並將軍事行動納入塞族共和國的政治架構。拉特科·姆拉迪奇是前線最具決定性的指揮官之一，他將南軍骨幹、地方部隊、砲兵與後勤系統編入塞族共和國軍，後來出任該軍最高指揮官；原南軍第二軍區指揮官日沃科·佩特科維奇則代表早期聯邦指揮鏈。波黑軍初期的組織工作主要由塞費爾·哈利洛維奇負責，地方指揮仍高度分散，至9月由拉西姆·德利奇接任，並著重整軍團與旅級指揮體系。克羅埃西亞總統弗蘭約·圖赫曼決定對外戰略方向，軍方則由揚科·博貝特科策劃西部戰區行動。這些人物在1992年並非始終保持一致，其正式職稱與實際影響也時有出入；戰局正是在這種政治目標、聯邦軍制與地方軍權互相重疊的情況下展開。
peopleEn: Command in Bosnia remained divided among political leaders, chiefs of staff, and former Yugoslav commanders. Alija Izetbegović, chairman of the Bosnian Presidency, represented the state's constitutional goal of remaining unified. Radovan Karadžić led the establishment of Serb political institutions and placed military operations within the political structure of Republika Srpska. Ratko Mladić was among the most consequential front-line commanders: he integrated the Yugoslav officer corps, local formations, artillery, and logistics into the Army of Republika Srpska and later became its supreme commander. Živko Petković, formerly commander of the Yugoslav People's Army's 2nd Corps, represented the federal chain of command during the opening phase. Sefer Halilović organized the initial Bosnian Army staff, although local command remained highly fragmented; in September he was replaced by Rasim Delić, who concentrated on reorganizing corps and brigade command. Franjo Tuđman defined Croatia's strategic direction, while Janko Bobetko planned operations in the western theater. These figures did not exercise consistent influence throughout 1992, and their formal titles did not always match their actual authority. The war unfolded precisely because political aims, federal military structures, and local armed power overlapped.
kits: 截至1992年，交戰各方的軍械仍以1992年前已列裝的裝備為主。南軍與塞族共和國軍可使用M-84主力戰車、BVP M-84步兵戰車、LOVA M-86裝甲偵察車，以及M-84 130毫米榴彈炮、M-87 152毫米榴彈炮、D-30與M-24 122毫米榴彈炮；同一M-84名稱分別出現在坦克、砲兵與槍械系統，不能混為一型。步兵火力包括Zastava M84 7.62毫米步槍、M70與M80 7.62毫米步槍、Zastava M84 12.7毫米通用機槍、RPG-7火箭筒及9K11 Malyutka線導反裝甲飛彈。空中裝備主要有MiG-21bis戰鬥機與Mi-8、Mi-17直升機，但空襲和偵察活動很快受到聯合國觀察與禁運的約束。波黑政府與克羅埃西亞國防委員會使用由克羅埃西亞轉交的原南軍裝備、原有軍械庫及作戰中繳得的車輛，火炮包括D-30、M-24、M-84與M-87；波黑軍另接收一批1992年以前已列裝的中國Type 69坦克。火力消耗集中在122毫米、130毫米與152毫米炮彈、坦克115毫米穿甲彈，以及7.62×39毫米與7.62×51毫米步機槍彈藥。聯合國禁運限制新供應與備件，卻未能立即消除各方原有庫存，後勤差異主要表現在砲彈補充速度、柴油、輪胎與車隊維修能力。
kitsEn: By 1992, the opposing forces were still overwhelmingly equipped with weapons fielded before that year. The Yugoslav People's Army and the Army of Republika Srpska could field the M-84 main battle tank, BVP M-84 infantry fighting vehicle, LOVA M-86 reconnaissance vehicle, M-84 130 mm howitzer, M-87 152 mm howitzer, and D-30 and M-24 122 mm howitzers. The M-84 designation applied to several unrelated systems in the tank, artillery, and small-arms categories and therefore could not be treated as a single weapon. Infantry weapons included the Zastava M84 7.62 mm rifle, M70 and M80 7.62 mm rifles, Zastava M84 12.7 mm general-purpose machine gun, RPG-7 launcher, and 9K11 Malyutka wire-guided anti-tank missile. Aviation equipment centered on the MiG-21bis fighter and Mi-8 and Mi-17 helicopters, although air strikes and reconnaissance were increasingly constrained by United Nations observation and the embargo. Bosnian government and Croatian Defence Council formations used former Yugoslav equipment transferred by Croatia, existing depots, and vehicles recovered during operations. Their artillery included the D-30, M-24, M-84, and M-87, while the Bosnian Army also received a batch of Chinese Type 69 tanks, a model fielded well before 1992. Ammunition expenditure centered on 122 mm, 130 mm, and 152 mm rounds, 115 mm tank ammunition, and 7.62×39 mm and 7.62×51 mm rifle and machine-gun ammunition. The United Nations embargo restricted new deliveries and spare parts but did not immediately remove existing stocks. The principal logistical differences therefore lay in the speed of artillery resupply, diesel supply, tires, and maintenance capacity rather than in a sudden lack of artillery.
tactics: 4月開戰時，塞族共和國軍與南軍通常沿公路和河谷軸線推進，以步兵掩護裝甲車，砲兵先射擊道路交會點與政府軍陣位，工兵則處理路障和橋梁障礙。波黑軍初期缺乏統一車輛與重火力，因而更多依靠步兵固守、側翼反擊、反裝甲伏擊、夜間移動及短程迫擊砲火力。沙拉熱窩失守外圍交通樞紐後，戰鬥由機動戰轉為壕溝、射擊掩體、 sniper fire與砲兵交戰；控制伊格曼山、別拉什尼察山、特雷貝維奇山和亞霍里納山等高地的一方，可從較高射界監視盆地內道路與集結區，砲兵也因反砲兵壓力而反覆轉移陣位。6月底至7月的走廊92行動中，波黑軍與克羅埃西亞國防委員會部隊沿波蘇什耶方向建立先頭部隊、工兵與後勤車隊，但裝甲車與步兵協同不足，最終未能形成通往沙拉熱窩的永久通道。9月至11月，比哈奇戰區出現蜘蛛行動、馬德耶維察戰役、利瓦達戰役與烏納行動，塞族共和國軍企圖封鎖盆地出口，波黑軍及克羅埃西亞部隊則反覆奪回山脊和公路。兩軍後來建立共同防線，卻在指揮權、部隊番號及邊界控制上出現摩擦。全年補給主要依靠公路車隊與原軍械庫，鐵路屢遭破壞，砲彈按射擊任務配給，直升機只承擔緊急人員與物資輸送。
tacticsEn: When the war began in April, the Army of Republika Srpska and Yugoslav People's Army formations usually advanced along roads and river valleys, using infantry to cover armor while artillery fired on road junctions and government positions. Engineers dealt with barricades and damaged crossings. The Bosnian Army initially lacked unified transport and heavy firepower, so it relied more on infantry positions, flank reactions, anti-tank ambushes, night movement, and short-range mortar fire. Once the approaches to Sarajevo had fallen, the battle changed from maneuver into a struggle involving trenches, firing positions, sniper fire, and artillery duels. Control of the heights around Igman, Bjelašnica, Trebević, and Jahorina gave the possessing force observation over roads and assembly areas inside the basin, while counterbattery pressure forced guns to move repeatedly between firing positions. During Operation Corridor 92 from late June through July, Bosnian and Croatian Defence Council units formed leading infantry, engineer, and logistics columns toward Posušje, but inadequate coordination between armor and infantry prevented them from opening a permanent route to Sarajevo. Between September and November, Operation Spider, the fighting around Mađevica and Livada, and Operation Una shaped the Bihać sector. Republika Srpska forces sought to close the exits from the basin, while Bosnian and Croatian units repeatedly recaptured ridges and roads. The two allies later established common defensive lines but developed friction over command, unit designations, and control of boundaries. Throughout the year, logistics depended on road convoys and existing depots because the railways were repeatedly damaged. Artillery ammunition was allocated by mission, while helicopters carried only urgent personnel and cargo.
data: 可核對的時間線如下：1992年3月1日，波黑舉行獨立公投，官方統計顯示投票率約七成，贊成者占已投票者的絕大多數；2月21日通過的聯合國安全理事會第743號決議則授權部署約一萬四千人的聯合國保護區部隊。4月5日至6日，沙拉熱窩的武裝衝突擴大，6日波黑主席團宣布獨立，7日獲歐洲共同體與美國承認，9日塞族方面宣布成立波斯尼亞塞族自治區。4月下旬的科沙雷戰鬥阻止南軍越過德里納河擴張。5月20日前後，南軍完成主要撤離並解散，塞族共和國軍正式承接其裝備；5月22日，第757號決議實施全面武器禁運。5月至6月，南軍與塞族共和國軍對杜布羅夫尼克發動攻勢，但未突破克羅埃西亞防線。6月27日至7月24日，波黑軍與克羅埃西亞國防委員會實施走廊92，推進至波蘇什耶後未能打通沙拉熱窩。9月至10月，蜘蛛行動、馬德耶維察戰役與利瓦達戰役在比哈奇盆地交錯；10月26日，波斯尼亞克萊迪納自治區成立，11月烏納行動恢復通往克羅埃西亞方向的公路，10月塞族共和國軍亦控制亞布拉尼察，切斷沙拉熱窩西南鐵路樞紐。12月各方仍嘗試局部停火，聯合國外交工作則在1993年1月形成萬斯—歐文的停火方案。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology is as follows. On 1 March 1992, Bosnia held an independence referendum. Official figures showed a turnout of roughly seventy percent, with the great majority of those voting favoring independence. On 21 February, United Nations Security Council Resolution 743 had authorized the deployment of approximately 14,000 peacekeepers. Fighting in Sarajevo expanded on 5 and 6 April. The Presidency declared independence on 6 April, recognition by the European Community and the United States followed on 7 April, and the Serb side proclaimed the Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Bosnia and Herzegovina on 9 April. The fighting at Košare in late April prevented a Yugoslav Army crossing of the Drina from expanding. Around 20 May, the Yugoslav People's Army completed its principal withdrawal and was dissolved, with the Army of Republika Srpska formally inheriting its equipment. On 22 May, Resolution 757 imposed a comprehensive arms embargo. From May through June, Yugoslav and Republika Srpska forces attacked Dubrovnik but failed to break the Croatian defensive line. Between 27 June and 24 July, Bosnian and Croatian Defence Council forces conducted Operation Corridor 92, reaching Posušje without opening a route to Sarajevo. Operation Spider and the fighting around Mađevica and Livada overlapped in the Bihać basin from September to October. On 26 October, the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia was proclaimed. Operation Una restored the road toward Croatia in November, while Republika Srpska forces took Jablanica in October, severing the southwestern rail junction from Sarajevo. Local ceasefires were still attempted in December, and the United Nations diplomatic work produced the Vance-Owen cease-fire proposals in January 1993.
cause: 戰爭的直接背景是南斯拉夫聯邦在斯洛維尼亞與克羅埃西亞獨立戰爭後解體，而波斯尼亞的國家機構尚未完成權力重組。1990年地方選舉使三個主要政黨分別掌握不同政治動員網絡；其後的制憲爭議未能建立各方接受的軍隊與警察權威安排。塞族民主黨建立平行地方機構，尋求自治或與聯邦重新連結；克羅埃西亞國防委員會在西部形成自己的軍隊；波黑主席團與波黑軍則堅持維持統一的主權國家。南斯拉夫人民軍仍掌握波黑境內的營區、裝甲、砲兵與軍事任命權，使聯邦指揮鏈在4月成為決定性的變量。3月公投、外部承認與4月塞族自治區宣告相繼發生，使原本可由談判處理的制度衝突迅速軍事化。當南軍部隊與塞族武裝共同進攻沙拉熱窩時，波黑政府的統一軍令尚不完整，克羅埃西亞支持的國防委員會又與政府軍存在目標差異，西部防線因而與 Sarajevo 戰線同時惡化。聯合國武器禁運在5月才全面生效，因此不是開戰的最初原因；但原有軍備仍留在本地，外部補充受限，使衝突得以延續。種族與政治分裂是結構條件，真正把爭議轉成戰爭的則是組織、指揮和進攻決策。
causeEn: The immediate background was the dissolution of the Yugoslav federation after the wars over Slovenian and Croatian independence, while Bosnia's state institutions had not completed a reorganization of authority. Local elections in 1990 produced three principal party networks with different bases of political mobilization. Subsequent constitutional disputes failed to establish a military and police authority acceptable to every party. The Serbian Democratic Party created parallel local institutions in search of autonomy or renewed federation. The Croatian Defence Council formed its own army in the west, while the Bosnian Presidency and Bosnian Army sought to preserve a unified sovereign state. The Yugoslav People's Army still controlled barracks, armor, artillery, and military appointments in Bosnia, making the federal chain of command the decisive variable in April. The March referendum, external recognition, and the April proclamation of the Serb autonomous region transformed a constitutional dispute that might still have been negotiated into an armed conflict. When Yugoslav Army formations and Serb forces jointly attacked Sarajevo, the Bosnian government's unified command structure remained incomplete, and the Croatia-backed Croatian Defence Council differed from the government army over objectives, causing the western front to deteriorate alongside the Sarajevo front. The United Nations arms embargo did not take full effect until May and therefore was not the original cause of the war. Existing weapons nevertheless remained in the region, while external replenishment became restricted, allowing the conflict to continue. Ethnic and political division formed the structural conditions, but organization, command, and decisions to attack converted those divisions into war.
impact: 1992年的最大戰略影響，是南軍在5月主要撤出後，衝突從聯邦軍介入迅速轉成波黑政府軍、塞族共和國軍與克羅埃西亞國防委員會三方競逐；原南軍的裝甲、砲兵、軍官與後勤網絡則大部轉入塞族共和國軍，使其能在不依賴聯邦指揮的情況下持續攻勢。武器禁運切斷新的外部供應、備件與較新型裝備流入，但各方原有軍械庫仍足以維持每日砲戰，因此禁運初期只改變補給條件，未能壓低戰爭強度。沙拉熱窩方面，走廊92未能形成永久突破線，亞布拉尼察又落入塞族共和國軍控制，城市西南鐵路與縱深補給持續受壓；控制周邊高地的一方則能以砲兵和狙擊火力約束政府軍行動。西部方面，蜘蛛行動一度使比哈奇與克羅埃西亞方向接近中斷，馬德耶維察、利瓦達和烏納等連續反擊則迫使塞族共和國軍分兵回援，十一月恢復通往波萊尼亞克萊迪納的公路，使比哈奇戰區得以維持與克羅埃西亞的連繫。克羅埃西亞軍隊由杜布羅夫尼克方向進一步投入波斯尼亞西部，使戰爭與克羅埃西亞本土防務更難分開。波黑軍與克羅埃西亞國防委員會雖建立共同防線，卻在指揮和地區利益上開始摩擦。聯合國保護區部隊實際上多在觀察局部停火與維持接觸線，未能執行全面解除武裝。
impactEn: The principal strategic effect of 1992 was the rapid transformation of the conflict from a federal military intervention into a three-way struggle among the Bosnian government forces, the Army of Republika Srpska, and the Croatian Defence Council. With the main Yugoslav Army withdrawal in May, its armor, artillery, officer corps, and logistics network largely passed to Republika Srpska, allowing the latter to sustain offensive operations without the federal chain of command. The arms embargo restricted new deliveries, spare parts, and more modern equipment, but existing depots remained sufficient for daily artillery duels. The embargo therefore initially changed supply conditions rather than reducing the intensity of combat. Around Sarajevo, Operation Corridor 92 failed to create a permanent breakthrough route, while the loss of Jablanica placed continued pressure on the southwestern railway and deeper supply lines. Whichever side controlled the surrounding heights could constrain government movements through artillery and sniper fire. In the west, Operation Spider brought Bihać close to being cut off from Croatia, but the counterattacks around Mađevica and Livada and Operation Una forced Republika Srpska forces to redirect troops and recover the road toward Bosanska Krajina in November, preserving the western connection. Croatian forces entered western Bosnia more deeply after the Dubrovnik fighting, making the Bosnian and Croatian theaters increasingly difficult to separate. Bosnian government and Croatian Defence Council troops formed common defensive lines but also developed friction over command and regional interests. The United Nations Protection Force mostly observed local ceasefires and maintained contact lines rather than carrying out comprehensive disarmament.
result: 截至1992年12月，沒有一方取得足以決定戰爭的戰術或戰略成果。塞族共和國軍控制波斯尼亞東部與東北部大片地區，並從東側及東南側壓縮沙拉熱窩；波黑政府軍與克羅埃西亞國防委員會聯盟維持中部、西部及西南部的主要聯繫區，波黑方面也保住比哈奇與波斯尼亞克萊迪納通向克羅埃西亞的道路。走廊92未能打開通往沙拉熱窩的永久補給走廊，蜘蛛行動造成的比哈奇孤立則在烏納行動後解除，沙拉熱窩封鎖仍在繼續。聯邦層面的南軍已不再是主要參戰者，但塞族共和國軍完整承接其重裝備與指揮經驗，使外國軍隊直接介入的重要性下降；波黑軍在德利奇接手後完成初步軍團化，仍缺乏足以壓倒塞族砲兵與裝甲部隊的集中力量。聯合國禁運、保護區部隊與局部停火維持了有限接觸，卻未形成全國性停火協議。1993年1月推出的萬斯—歐文方案以軍事停火及 canton 劃分作為談判框架，執行仍迅速受阻。因而這場1992年戰役最後形成的不是勝負，而是各方守住既有陣線、政府軍得以重整、塞族軍保有既有裝備、聯合國介入由觀察走向有限斡旋的僵持局面；整場波斯尼亞戰爭則繼續延至1995年。
resultEn: By December 1992, no side had achieved a tactical or strategic result capable of deciding the war. The Army of Republika Srpska held extensive areas of eastern and northeastern Bosnia and compressed Sarajevo from the east and southeast. The Bosnian government and Croatian Defence Council alliance retained the principal links through central, western, and southwestern Bosnia, while the Bosnian side also preserved the road linking Bihać and Bosanska Krajina to Croatia. Operation Corridor 92 had failed to open a permanent supply corridor to Sarajevo, but the isolation of Bihać produced by Operation Spider was relieved by Operation Una, while the siege of Sarajevo continued. The federal Yugoslav Army was no longer the principal belligerent, yet Republika Srpska had inherited its heavy equipment and command experience, reducing the importance of direct foreign military intervention. Under Rasim Delić, the Bosnian Army completed an initial transition to a corps-based structure, but it still lacked the concentrated power needed to defeat Republika Srpska artillery and armor. The United Nations embargo, the protection force, and local ceasefires maintained limited contact but did not produce a nationwide armistice. The Vance-Owen proposals introduced in January 1993 placed a military ceasefire and canton-based arrangements on the negotiating agenda, but implementation soon stalled. The 1992 campaign therefore ended not in a decision but in a military stalemate: each side held its existing lines, the government forces reorganized, Republika Srpska retained its heavy weapons, and United Nations involvement shifted from observation toward limited mediation. The wider Bosnian War continued until 1995.
